page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-64 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on x86_64 architecture. It provides 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at a base frequency of 3.0 GHz. The processor configuration includes a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 4 MB L2 cache, and a 16 MB L3 cache. It incorporates advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI, which accelerate specialized vector and cryptographic computations.

The system is allocated 64 GB of system memory, establishing a 2 GB memory-per-vCPU ratio. In benchmark evaluations, the memory subsystem demonstrates high throughput, achieving strong top-quartile performance in PassMark memory testing alongside uncached large-block read rates of 150.63 GB/s. CPU performance falls consistently in the median tier across general compute benchmarks, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,539 and a PassMark CPU rating of 36,294.15. Vectorized image processing and lightweight model text generation also reflect top-quartile results, buoyed by the underlying Intel hardware extensions.

Hardware tradeoffs for this instance include the total absence of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators, as it includes zero GPUs. All operational storage requirements depend entirely on remote block volumes or network-attached filesystems. Network resources include one complimentary public IPv4 address. Given its dedicated core allocation and balanced high clock-speed execution, VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-64 delivers stable resource density for high-throughput batch processing, software compilation pipelines, API serving, and compute-bound algorithmic tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.16-64 is a compute-oriented instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at 3.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. It delivers 16 physical cores and 32 dedicated vCPUs paired with 64 GB of system memory, providing a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Architectural extensions include AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and cryptographic acceleration. Benchmarks reflect solid median multi-core compute capability, accompanied by top-quartile PassMark memory marks and accelerated image processing. The instance contains zero GPUs and features no local instance storage, requiring remote block storage for persistent volumes. It includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated compute allocation and strong memory subsystem suit this configuration for continuous integration pipelines, batch data processing, distributed compiling, and computationally demanding web service tiers.
